title: System Architecture: Foundations
welcome_lead: Meet the von Neumann architecture — the blueprint of nearly every computer.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science adventure on von Neumann architecture and CPU components.
final_note: You now know the core design behind nearly every computer ever built.

concepts.def: Stores data and instructions in same memory.
Arithmetic logic unit — does maths and logic.
Control unit — directs the CPU's actions.
Main memory holding programs and data in use.
Input and output devices, e.g. keyboard, screen.

walkthroughs.body_html: Before von Neumann, instructions and data were stored separately. His idea: store both in the same memory. This makes computers flexible — load any program into RAM and run it.

• ALU does sums and logic
  • CU fetches and decodes instructions
  • Registers hold values in use
  • Cache stores recent data for speed
RAM is fast but volatile — loses content when power is off. The OS loads programs from storage into RAM so the CPU can run them.
